Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri R.P. Srivastava (AOR No.1557/2012) holding brief of Sri Pradeep Kumar Tiwari,
learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.K. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State/opposite party no.1.
2.

This application under Section 528 of the BNSS has been filed by the applicant to quash the Non Bailable Warrant dated 6.2.2025 + 82 Cr.P.C. passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-VIII, Agra in Case No. 3367 of 2009 (State Vs. Sabal Singh and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 163 of 2006, under Sections 366, 376 LP.C., Police Station-Etmaddaula,
District-Agra.

entities.text: Case No. 3367 of 2009 (State Vs. Sabal Singh and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that though the applicant confines his relief only for a direction for enlargement on bail.

4. Learned AGA has invited attention of the Court towards Annexure-7 at page 40 of the paper book reference whereof has made in para 16 of the application being order dated 19.11.2019 in Application Sanjana vs State Of U.P. on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118236343/
1 U/S 482 Cr.P.C.No. 40883 of 2019 (Narayan Singh and another Vs. State of U.P. and another)
wherein the following order has been passed:-
"1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Narayan Singh and another Vs. State of U.P. and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the order dated 20.02.2017 and 15.06.2019 by which the Non- Bailable Warrants issued against the applicant as well as the entire proceedings of Case No. 3009 of 2006 (State Vs. Sabal Singh and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 163 of 2006, under Sections- 366 I.P.C., Police Station- Etmaddaula, District- Agra, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-10th, Agra.
3.

entities.text: Case No. 3009 of 2006 (State Vs. Sabal Singh and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that no offence against the applicants is disclosed and the present prosecution has been instituted with a malafide intention for the purpose of causing harassment.
He pointed out certain documents and statements in support of his contention.
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the applicants and perused the materials brought on record, it does not appear to be a fit case to quash the impugned order.

The prayer to quash the same is hereby refused, at this stage as the argument raised by learned counsel for the applicants involves factual disputes and appraisal of evidence.
5.

However, looking at the nature of offence alleged and attending facts and circumstances of the case, as have been brought on record, it is directed that if the applicants appear and surrender before the court below within 30 days from today and apply for bail, their prayer for bail shall be considered and decided in view of the settled law laid by this Court in the case of Amrawati and another Vs. State of U.P.
reported in 2004 (57) ALR 290 as well as judgement passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2009 (3) ADJ 322 (SC) Lal Kamlendra Pratap Singh Vs. State of U.P.
6.

entities.text:
Amrawati and another Vs. State of U.P.
reported in 2004 (57) ALR 290
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: 2009 (3) ADJ 322 (SC) Lal Kamlendra Pratap Singh Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For a period of 30 days from today, the non-bailable warrant issued against the applicants shall be kept in abeyance.
7. The present application stands disposed of."
5. Learned AGA further submits that the present application may not be maintainable on the same cause of action.
6. Be that as it may be, it is always open for the applicant to take legal recourse which is permissible under law.
The application stands disposed of.
7. Passing of this order may not be construed that this Court has adjudicated the matter on merits.
